description: Re-sign the bun --compile binary ad-hoc at build/install time so it runs anywhere on macOS (fixes /usr/local/bin SIGKILL), plus a user-owned --install flag and README update.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: bun build --compile has no built-in signing on macOS; docs recommend running codesign manually after compile. Ad-hoc re-sign (codesign --force --sign -) is supported on Bun >= 1.2.4 and yields a binary that codesign -v accepts. JIT entitlements are only needed under hardened runtime / Developer ID, not for ad-hoc signing. The documented target string is bun-darwin-arm64.

userStories.title: Ad-hoc re-sign the compiled binary in build-release.sh
userStories.description: As a cam-cli maintainer, I need scripts/build-release.sh to re-sign the freshly compiled binary ad-hoc and verify the signature so the artifact runs without amfid SIGKILL in any destination directory (including /usr/local/bin), eliminating the 'zsh: killed' failure observed during US-010 smoke.
acceptanceCriteria: After `bun build --compile` and before the size/--version checks, scripts/build-release.sh runs `codesign --force --sign - "${BIN}"`.
Immediately after re-signing, scripts/build-release.sh runs `codesign -v "${BIN}"`; on failure it prints a clear error and exits 1.
On success the script logs `[build-release] codesign: ad-hoc re-sign ok` (matching the existing `[build-release] ...` log style).
codesign is invoked unconditionally (the script is darwin-only via `stat -f`); no platform branching is added.
`bash -n scripts/build-release.sh` passes (syntax check).
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck).
Tests pass (bun test).
userStories.notes: File to edit: scripts/build-release.sh. Insert the re-sign + verify block between the existing `bun build --compile ...` line (~line 51) and the `--- Sanity: AC2 (size) ---` block (~line 53). Use the existing `${BIN}` variable. Keep `set -euo pipefail` behavior intact; prefer an explicit `|| { echo ...; exit 1; }` for a clearer error message, matching the existing error-handling style in the script. Background: lessons.md 2026-06-06 entry (lines 25-31): without re-sign, the binary's signature reads invalid and amfid kills it in /usr/local/bin. Do not add any feature beyond re-sign + verify in this story; --install lives in US-002.

userStories.title: Add --install [dest] flag to build-release.sh (user-owned default)
userStories.description: As a cam-cli operator on macOS, I need `./scripts/build-release.sh --install` to copy the freshly built binary to a user-owned destination (default ~/.local/bin/cam), strip quarantine, re-sign ad-hoc, and smoke-test --version so I get a working binary without sudo and without hitting the /usr/local/bin amfid trap.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/build-release.sh accepts `--install` and optionally a positional path immediately after it (e.g. `--install ~/.local/bin/cam`).
When --install is absent, current behavior is unchanged (build + sign + size + --version checks).
Default destination when no path is given: `${HOME}/.local/bin/cam`.
The parent directory of the destination is created with `mkdir -p` before copying.
After copy: run `xattr -cr "${DEST}"` (clears any quarantine attribute; inocuous on a freshly built local binary).
After xattr: run `codesign --force --sign - "${DEST}"` and then `codesign -v "${DEST}"`; on verify failure, exit 1 with a clear error.
Smoke step: invoke `"${DEST}" --version`, compare against `cam ${VERSION}` (same VERSION the script already parses from src/version.ts); on mismatch, exit 1 with a clear error.
If the directory containing the destination is not on `$PATH`, print a warning (warning only, do not fail).

The script's Usage header (the `#` block at the top, currently rendered by `grep '^#' "$0" | head -16`) is updated to document `--install [dest]`; bump the `head -N` count if needed so the new lines render under `-h`.
The arg parser still rejects unknown args with exit 2 (existing behavior preserved).
`bash -n scripts/build-release.sh` passes (syntax check).
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck).
Tests pass (bun test).
userStories.notes: File to edit: scripts/build-release.sh. The current arg loop uses `for arg in "$@"; do case "$arg" in ...`, which iterates per-arg and cannot consume the optional positional after --install. Switch to a `while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do case "$1" in ... esac; shift; done` loop so `--install` can peek `$2`, consume it with `shift`, and still keep `-h|--help` and the unknown-arg `*) exit 2` behavior. Keep the existing -h/--help grep-the-header trick; just update the comment block at the top to include the new flag and bump the `head -16` count to cover the full new Usage block (likely `head -20`; count the `#` lines after editing so the help renders the whole Usage section and nothing below it). Use `case ":${PATH}:" in *":${DEST_DIR}:"*) ;; *) echo warning ;; esac` for the PATH membership check (POSIX-safe, no external tools). Background: lessons.md 2026-06-06 entry (lines 25-31). Do NOT create a `cam install` TS subcommand; operator-approved scope keeps install as a bash flag. Do NOT add Developer ID / notarytool logic; that is README-only (US-004).

userStories.title: Operator smoke: verify --install flow on a real macOS box and replace stale /usr/local/bin/cam
userStories.description: As the cam-cli operator, I need to verify on my actual machine that `./scripts/build-release.sh --install` produces a working `~/.local/bin/cam` whose signature codesign accepts, and to retire or overwrite the stale `/usr/local/bin/cam` left over from the unsigned-binary era, so dogfooding stops hitting the amfid SIGKILL trap.
acceptanceCriteria: Run `./scripts/build-release.sh --install` on the operator's darwin-arm64 machine; it exits 0.
`~/.local/bin/cam --version` runs without hanging and prints `cam ${VERSION}` matching src/version.ts.
`codesign -v ~/.local/bin/cam` exits 0 (no 'code or signature have been modified' error).

The stale `/usr/local/bin/cam` is either deleted (operator decision A) or overwritten with the freshly signed binary via `sudo cp ~/.local/bin/cam /usr/local/bin/cam && sudo codesign --force --sign - /usr/local/bin/cam && codesign -v /usr/local/bin/cam` (operator decision B); operator records which path was taken.
Operator confirms `which cam` resolves to the intended binary (either `~/.local/bin/cam` after PATH precedence, or the rebuilt `/usr/local/bin/cam`).
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck).
Tests pass (bun test).
userStories.notes: Real-machine verification. Cannot be automated: needs the operator's $PATH, $HOME, possibly sudo, and decision on what to do with the legacy /usr/local/bin/cam binary. References: lessons.md 2026-06-06 entry (lines 25-31) for the failure mode being verified; the stale-PATH-binary risk this also retires. Implementer should treat this story as out-of-scope and let the loop fall through to US-004.

userStories.title: README: update build/install section for re-sign + user-owned install and add Developer ID note
userStories.description: As a new cam-cli user reading the README, I need the install instructions to reflect the re-signed binary and the user-owned `--install` flow (no sudo by default), plus a brief note on what production-grade public distribution would require, so I do not hit the /usr/local/bin amfid trap and so I understand the limits of the current ad-hoc signing.
acceptanceCriteria: README.md Install section, Option A (from source), reflects that the release build now produces a re-signed binary (one short sentence is enough) and recommends `./scripts/build-release.sh --install` for the user-owned default at `~/.local/bin/cam` (no sudo).
README documents that `~/.local/bin` must be on `$PATH` (one line, e.g. mention adding it to the shell rc if missing).

The previous `sudo cp ... /usr/local/bin/cam` recipe is either removed or kept as a clearly labeled alternative that notes the destination requires the binary to be signed (which the build script now handles).

A short subsection (or note) titled around 'Public distribution' explains that wider distribution would require Developer ID signing + notarytool + stapler and an Apple Developer account, and that the current ad-hoc signing is sufficient only for the user's own machine.
No em-dash appears in the edits to README.md; use colon, comma, parens, or period instead (hard project rule).
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck).
Tests pass (bun test).
